column1: 1:1|Solomon son of David strengthened his hold on his kingdom. The LORD his God was with him and made him exceedingly great.|Keep royal consolidation and divine presence as distinct opening claims.
1:2|Solomon spoke to all Israel: the commanders of thousands and hundreds, the judges, and every leader in Israel, the heads of ancestral houses.|Preserve every leadership category addressed.

1:3|Solomon and the whole assembly with him went to the high place at Gibeon. God’s tent of meeting was there, the one Moses the LORD’s servant had made in the wilderness.|Keep the gathering’s destination and the tent’s Mosaic provenance.

1:4|David, however, had brought God’s ark up from Kiriath-jearim to the place he had prepared for it, for he had pitched a tent for it in Jerusalem.|Distinguish the ark’s tent in Jerusalem from the tent at Gibeon.

1:5|The bronze altar made by Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, stood before the LORD’s tabernacle. Solomon and the assembly sought the LORD there.|Choose the LORD as the object of seeking while noting that the pronoun may refer to the altar.
1:6|Solomon went up there to the bronze altar before the LORD at the tent of meeting and presented a thousand burnt offerings on it.|Retain the exact offering count and altar setting.
1:7|That night God appeared to Solomon and said, “Ask what I should give you.”|Preserve appearance without adding Kings’ dream terminology.
1:8|Solomon said to God, “You have shown great faithful love to my father David and have made me king in his place.|Keep faithful love connected to succession.
1:9|Now, LORD God, let your word to my father David stand firm. You have made me king over a people as numerous as the dust of the earth.|Preserve the promise and dust image.
1:10|Give me wisdom and knowledge so I can go out and come in before this people. For who can govern this great people of yours?”|Retain the leadership movement image and both wisdom terms.

1:11|God said to Solomon, “Because this was in your heart, and you did not ask for wealth, possessions, honor, the lives of those who hate you, or even many years of life, but asked for wisdom and knowledge to govern my people over whom I made you king,|Keep every unrequested benefit and the motive stated by God.

1:12|wisdom and knowledge are given to you. I will also give you wealth, possessions, and honor such as no king before you has had and none after you will have.”|Preserve the granted request and the additional unparalleled gifts.

1:13|Solomon came from the high place at Gibeon, from before the tent of meeting, to Jerusalem, and he reigned over Israel.|Render the difficult directional wording according to the departure context and note the Hebrew problem.

1:14|Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen. He had fourteen hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen, which he stationed in the chariot towns and with the king in Jerusalem.|Keep both totals and both stationing locations.
1:15|The king made silver and gold as common in Jerusalem as stones, and cedar as plentiful as the sycamore figs in the foothills.|Retain both metals and both abundance comparisons.

1:16|Solomon’s horses were imported from Egypt and Kue. The king’s merchants bought them from Kue at the going price.|Choose the place-name Kue while flagging the alternative understanding of the difficult trade term.

1:17|They imported a chariot from Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver and a horse for a hundred fifty. Through these merchants they also exported them to all the Hittite and Aramean kings.|Supply the customary silver unit and preserve both prices and export destinations.
2:1|Solomon decided to build a house for the LORD’s name and a house for his own kingdom.|Bind this public verse to Hebrew 1:18 and retain the paired houses.

2:2|He counted out seventy thousand men to carry loads, eighty thousand to quarry stone in the hills, and thirty-six hundred to supervise them.|Bind Hebrew 2:1 and preserve all three workforce figures.

2:3|Solomon sent this message to Huram king of Tyre: “Deal with me as you did with my father David, when you sent him cedar to build a house to live in.|Supply the request implicit in the comparison while retaining the earlier relationship.

2:4|I am building a house for the name of the LORD my God, to dedicate it to him: to burn fragrant incense before him, to set out bread continually, and to present burnt offerings morning and evening, on Sabbaths, new moons, and the appointed festivals of the LORD our God. This is Israel’s lasting obligation.|Keep all worship actions, calendar occasions, and permanence.
2:5|The house I am building will be great, because our God is greater than all gods.|Preserve Solomon’s comparison and architectural conclusion.

2:6|But who has the strength to build him a house? Even heaven and the highest heavens cannot contain him. Who am I to build him a house, except as a place to burn offerings before him?|Keep the rhetorical limits on the temple’s ability to contain God.

2:7|Now send me a man skilled in working with gold, silver, bronze, iron, purple, crimson, and blue fabrics, and skilled in engraving. He will work with the skilled workers my father David provided for me in Judah and Jerusalem.|Preserve every material and both groups of workers.

2:8|Send me cedar, cypress, and algum timber from Lebanon. I know your servants are skilled at cutting Lebanon’s timber. My servants will work with yours|Keep all three tree terms and the joint workforce, continuing the purpose into the next verse.
2:9|to prepare timber for me in abundance, because the house I am building will be great and extraordinary.|Retain the scale and stated reason for abundant timber.

2:10|I will give your servants, the woodcutters who fell the trees, twenty thousand cors of beaten wheat, twenty thousand cors of barley, twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil.”|Preserve all four equal quantities, distinct measures, and the difficult beaten-wheat description.
2:11|Huram king of Tyre replied in a letter sent to Solomon: “Because the LORD loves his people, he has made you their king.”|Keep the written medium and the people-centered explanation.

2:12|Huram also said, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth! He has given King David a wise son with insight and understanding, who will build a house for the LORD and a house for his own kingdom.|Preserve the foreign king’s blessing and the repeated two-house project.
2:13|I am sending Huram-abi, a skilled man with understanding.|Retain the craftsman’s name-title and distinguish him from the king.

2:14|His mother is from the daughters of Dan, and his father is a man of Tyre. He knows how to work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, wood, purple, blue, fine linen, and crimson, and how to do every kind of engraving and devise any design assigned to him. He will work with your skilled workers and those of my lord David your father.|Keep Dan rather than harmonizing Kings and preserve the full skills inventory.
2:15|Now let my lord send his servants the wheat, barley, oil, and wine he promised.|Retain all four provisions in the reply’s order.

2:16|We will cut as much timber from Lebanon as you need and bring it to you by sea in rafts to Joppa. You can take it up to Jerusalem.”|Preserve the sea route, named port, and division of transport responsibility.

2:17|Solomon counted all the foreign men living in the land of Israel, following the count his father David had made. There were 153,600.|Keep the counted population and exact total without presenting the labor as voluntary.

2:18|He assigned seventy thousand of them to carry loads, eighty thousand to quarry stone in the hills, and thirty-six hundred as supervisors to keep the people at work.|Retain every assignment and the coercive force of making the people work.

3:1|Solomon began building the LORD’s house in Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where the LORD had appeared to his father David, at the place David had prepared on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.|Supply the LORD as the appearance’s subject and preserve the full site identification.
3:2|He began building on the second day of the second month in the fourth year of his reign.|Supply day for the elliptical second and retain all date elements.

3:3|These were the foundation dimensions Solomon used for building God’s house, measured in cubits of the older standard: sixty cubits long and twenty cubits wide.|Keep the older cubit standard and both foundation dimensions.

3:4|The entrance hall across the front was twenty cubits long, matching the width of the house, and a hundred twenty cubits high. He overlaid its interior with pure gold.|Retain the Hebrew’s striking height and flag the twenty-cubit alternative without silently correcting it.
3:5|He paneled the main hall with cypress, overlaid it with fine gold, and decorated it with palm trees and chains.|Preserve the underlying wood, gold covering, and both decorative motifs.
3:6|He adorned the house with precious stones for beauty. The gold was gold from Parvaim.|Keep the ornamental purpose and uncertain gold provenance.
3:7|He overlaid the house—its beams, thresholds, walls, and doors—with gold, and carved cherubim on the walls.|Retain all structural elements and carved creatures.

3:8|He made the Most Holy Place twenty cubits long, across the width of the house, and twenty cubits wide. He overlaid it with six hundred talents of fine gold.|Keep the square dimensions and large gold weight.
3:9|The gold nails weighed fifty shekels. He also overlaid the upper rooms with gold.|Retain the stated aggregate weight without asserting each nail weighed fifty.
3:10|In the Most Holy Place he made two sculpted cherubim and overlaid them with gold.|Preserve two figures and the uncertain workmanship term at a general level.

3:11|Together the cherubim’s wings spanned twenty cubits. One wing of the first cherub was five cubits long and touched the wall of the house; its other wing was five cubits long and touched the other cherub’s wing.|Keep the total span and the first figure’s two contacts.

3:12|One wing of the other cherub was five cubits long and touched the other wall of the house; its other wing was five cubits long and joined the first cherub’s wing.|Preserve the mirrored geometry and each five-cubit wing.
3:13|The wings of these cherubim spread out twenty cubits. The cherubim stood on their feet, facing the main hall.|Keep standing posture and the outward-facing direction.
3:14|He made the curtain of blue, purple, crimson, and fine linen, and worked cherubim into it.|Retain every textile color and the woven imagery.

3:15|He made two pillars in front of the house, thirty-five cubits in length, with a capital five cubits high on top of each.|Keep thirty-five without adding each or combined where the Hebrew does not settle it.

3:16|He made chains in the inner sanctuary and placed them on top of the pillars. He made a hundred pomegranates and put them on the chains.|Retain the difficult inner-sanctuary wording and exact pomegranate count, with the alternative noted.

3:17|He erected the pillars in front of the temple, one on the right and one on the left. He named the right one Jachin and the left one Boaz.|Keep both relative positions and meaningful pillar names.
4:1|He made a bronze altar twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high.|Preserve all three altar dimensions.

4:2|He made the Sea of cast metal, round in shape, ten cubits from rim to rim and five cubits high. A measuring line thirty cubits long encircled it.|Keep the named Sea and the source’s diameter, height, and circumference without recalculating them.

4:3|Figures of oxen encircled it underneath, ten to a cubit, all around the Sea. The oxen were in two rows, cast in one piece with it.|Retain oxen rather than substituting Kings’ gourds and preserve the casting method.

4:4|It stood on twelve oxen: three facing north, three west, three south, and three east. The Sea rested above them, and all their hindquarters faced inward.|Keep every orientation and the inward-facing rear portions.

4:5|It was a handbreadth thick. Its rim was shaped like the rim of a cup, like a lily blossom. It could hold three thousand baths.|Retain thickness, both shape comparisons, and Chronicles’ three-thousand capacity.

4:6|He made ten basins, placing five on the right and five on the left, for washing. They rinsed the materials for the burnt offering in them, while the Sea was for the priests to wash in.|Distinguish sacrificial washing from priestly washing and preserve the five-plus-five arrangement.
4:7|He made ten gold lampstands according to their prescribed design and put them in the main hall, five on the right and five on the left.|Keep the design reference and symmetrical placement.
4:8|He made ten tables and put them in the main hall, five on the right and five on the left. He also made a hundred gold sprinkling bowls.|Retain both furnishing counts and table positions.
4:9|He made the priests’ courtyard, the great courtyard, and doors for the courtyard, and overlaid the doors with bronze.|Preserve the two courts and door covering.
4:10|He placed the Sea on the right side, toward the southeast.|Unfold the east-and-south orientation concisely while retaining right side.
4:11|Huram made the pots, shovels, and sprinkling bowls. So Huram finished the work he did for King Solomon in God’s house:|Follow Huram’s read form and introduce the concluding inventory.
4:12|the two pillars, the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars, and the two networks covering the two bowl-shaped capitals;|Preserve the nested two-part architectural inventory.

4:13|the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, two rows of pomegranates for each network covering the two bowl-shaped capitals on top of the pillars;|Retain the four-hundred total and two rows on each network.
4:14|the stands and the basins he made on the stands;|Keep both supporting and supported furnishings.
4:15|the one Sea and the twelve oxen beneath it;|Preserve the singular Sea and twelve supports.

4:16|and the pots, shovels, forks, and all their utensils. Huram-abi made these of polished bronze for King Solomon for the LORD’s house.|Keep all utensil categories, the craftsman’s title, and the polished metal.
4:17|The king had them cast in the clay ground of the Jordan plain, between Succoth and Zeredah.|Retain the casting location and Chronicles’ Zeredah name.
4:18|Solomon made all these utensils in such great quantities that the weight of the bronze was never determined.|Keep the abundance and unmeasured weight without inventing an amount.
4:19|Solomon also made all the furnishings for God’s house: the gold altar, the tables on which the bread of the Presence was placed,|Retain the gold altar and the distinctive bread name.
4:20|the lampstands and their lamps of pure gold, to burn as prescribed before the inner sanctuary,|Keep material, purpose, and sanctuary location.
4:21|the flowers, lamps, and tongs of gold—the purest gold—|Preserve all three items and the emphatic purity statement.

4:22|and the wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, dishes, and firepans of pure gold. The entrances of the house—the inner doors to the Most Holy Place and the doors to the main hall—were gold.|Keep all remaining utensils and both sets of doors.

5:1|When all Solomon’s work for the LORD’s house was finished, he brought in the things his father David had dedicated. He placed the silver, gold, and all the utensils in the treasuries of God’s house.|Preserve completion and the continuity with David’s gifts.

5:2|Then Solomon assembled Israel’s elders, all the tribal heads, and the leaders of the Israelite ancestral houses in Jerusalem, to bring the ark of the LORD’s covenant up from the City of David, that is, Zion.|Keep every leadership group and identify Zion without conflating the two locations.
5:3|All the men of Israel assembled before the king at the festival in the seventh month.|Preserve the male referent and the unnamed festival’s timing.
5:4|All Israel’s elders came, and the Levites lifted the ark.|Keep Levites as carriers here before the priests’ role in verse 7.

5:5|They brought up the ark, the tent of meeting, and all the holy utensils in the tent. The Levitical priests brought them up.|Render the adjacent priests-Levites phrase as Levitical priests while noting the alternative priests and Levites.

5:6|King Solomon and the whole congregation of Israel gathered with him before the ark, sacrificing so many sheep and cattle that they could not be counted or numbered.|Retain both counting terms and the unquantified abundance.

5:7|The priests brought the ark of the LORD’s covenant to its place in the inner sanctuary of the house, the Most Holy Place, beneath the wings of the cherubim.|Preserve the nested location and the priests as carriers into it.
5:8|The cherubim spread their wings over the ark’s place, covering the ark and its poles from above.|Keep both objects sheltered by the wings.

5:9|The poles were so long that their ends could be seen extending from the ark in front of the inner sanctuary, but they could not be seen from outside. It remains there to this day.|Retain the difficult from-the-ark wording and the narrator’s singular enduring referent.

5:10|There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets Moses had placed there at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the Israelites when they came out of Egypt.|Keep the restrictive contents statement and covenant setting.

5:11|The priests came out of the holy place. All the priests present had consecrated themselves, without regard to their divisions.|Unfold the parenthesis as a sentence and preserve the suspension of division distinctions.

5:12|All the Levitical singers—Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, their sons, and their relatives—stood east of the altar, dressed in fine linen, with cymbals, harps, and lyres. With them were a hundred twenty priests sounding trumpets.|Keep the full musical personnel, dress, location, instruments, and exact priest count.

5:13|The trumpeters and singers joined as one, making one sound of praise and thanksgiving to the LORD. They raised their voices with trumpets, cymbals, and musical instruments, praising the LORD: “For he is good; his faithful love lasts forever.” Then a cloud filled the house, the LORD’s house.|Preserve the repeated unity, recognizable refrain, and repeated house identification.
5:14|The priests could not remain standing to serve because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled God’s house.|Keep the physical inability to serve and the glory filling the sanctuary.
